name: Groundsmoke
article: Spellcraft – Cantrips and Orisons of the Academy of Apprentices

targetAreaEffect.value: One fire no larger than 5 square feet

description: An apprentice wizard is said to have devised this orison while traveling with an adventuring mentor, so the pair's campfires wouldn't give away their position to anything watching from above. Cast on a fire no larger than five square feet, it keeps the smoke from rising at all: instead the smoke rolls out along the ground and sinks away within about six inches of the flame. The effect lasts 8 hours, and neither a saving throw nor spell resistance applies.
note: Unofficial fan compilation (see file-level note); page not recoverable, only issue and article are citable.

name: Vengeful Mount
article: Spellcraft – Cantrips and Orisons of the Academy of Apprentices
description: This orison began as a petty feud between two rival apprentices: one owned a particularly fine horse and lorded it over her rival by riding it across their master's lands at every opportunity, until the other apprentice conjured this spell so often that the first could no longer mount the animal anywhere within sight of their tower. Cast with a riding crop or willow switch as a material component against one animal within close range (25 ft. + 5 ft./2 levels), it allows a Will save and spell resistance applies. On a failed save the animal becomes stubborn and hard to control: any creature currently mounted on it must immediately succeed at a Ride check, typically DC 10, or be thrown or otherwise fail to stay seated. The effect itself is instantaneous, so it's the moment of casting that risks unseating a rider rather than an ongoing difficulty.

name: Guiding Star
description: A mote of pale starlight descends from the sky to orbit the caster's head, shedding light equal to a candle. Ordered to seek a place the caster has visited before, it stops circling and points like a compass in that direction, hovering just inches away and holding that bearing for as long as the spell lasts (1 minute/level). It makes no adjustments for walls or obstructions, pointing straight through them rather than routing around, and it simply resumes orbiting harmlessly if given no destination, if the caster has never actually been to the named place, or if that place lies on another plane of existence entirely.
note: No 'Saving Throw'/'Spell Resistance' values were captured from this compendium's page-number-less extraction. Filled in as None/No on the basis that this is a Personal-range, Target: You self-transformation spell with no save-triggering effect in its own header mechanic (any subsequent attack made with the granted natural weapon or ability uses normal attack rolls, not a save, against its target) — the same pattern confirmed for the file's other self-buff entries. Flag for correction if the original issue text is ever tracked down.

name: Motes of Moonlight
description: Conjures a fixed beam of silvery light that the caster can extend from their position to any point within line of sight, in whatever direction they choose. The beam itself is a five-foot-wide line of bright illumination, with a band of shadowy illumination in the five feet around it. Once cast, the beam hangs motionless in the air for the full duration (1 hour/level) even if the caster moves away; it can be dismissed early but never redirected once it's up.

name: Stonemantle
article: Dust to Dust – Magic of the Earthborn

targetAreaEffect.value: One Tiny object per caster level (larger objects count against the same allotment)

description: Lends the resilience of stone to fragile objects, tinting each affected surface a faint, dull gray without otherwise changing its appearance. The caster can affect one Tiny or smaller object per caster level, or an equivalent number of larger objects using the same pool: a Small object counts as 2 Tiny objects, Medium as 4, Large as 8, Huge as 16, Gargantuan as 32, and Colossal as 64. Every object treated this way gains hardness 8 and 15 hit points per inch of thickness (unless its own values are already better, in which case those apply instead), plus a +5 bonus to the DC required to break it, unless the spell didn't actually raise its hardness. Material component a pinch of powdered marble.

name: Sun Father's Face
description: The caster's face and hair take on a brief golden radiance evoking the sun god Pelor, shedding light equal to a candle while their hair streams outward like rays of sunlight. Before making a single turn undead attempt or wild empathy check, the caster can call on that glow for a +4 sacred bonus, which must be declared before the roll it applies to; the effect itself lasts 1 minute or until that bonus is spent, whichever comes first.
note: No 'Saving Throw'/'Spell Resistance' values were captured from this compendium's page-number-less extraction. Flag for correction if the original issue text is ever tracked down.

name: Curse of the Gypsies
description: Speaking a vehement curse over a single target within close range, the caster marks it as an enemy of their people and of nature itself, choosing one of three permanent afflictions. Bad Luck forces the target to reroll (keeping the worse result) any time it rolls a natural 20 on a d20, which can deny it critical hits entirely unless it has some way to threaten a critical on a lower roll. Mark of the Gypsies brands an invisible arcane mark on the target's forehead, visible only to the caster's own kin (typically fewer than a hundred people related by blood or an equally strong bond); anyone who can see it recognizes the bearer as cursed and shunned, usually souring reactions by two steps and sometimes provoking outright hostility, and while detect magic or true seeing can also reveal the mark, someone who can't see it outright needs a DC 20 Knowledge (arcana) check to understand what it means. Unnatural Aura makes every animal within 30 feet, wild or domesticated, sense the target as wrong: they won't approach any closer and panic if forced to. None of the three effects can be dispelled, though a break enchantment, remove curse, limited wish, miracle, or wish can lift them. The spell and the means of casting it are closely guarded, known mostly to ancient families, druidic circles, and wandering peoples like the Vistani.

name: Morning Mists
description: Functions as obscuring mist, but at battlefield scale: the caster can center a fog bank a hundred feet across and twenty feet high anywhere within long range, choosing at the moment of casting whether it stays put or crawls outward at ten feet per round. Material component bloodstones worth 100 gp.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor. Per the compendium's own rules, war-descriptor spells like this one can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat (Great Fortitude, Iron Will, spellcaster level 3rd) — mechanically load-bearing, flagging for the DM.

functionsAs.note: No explicit book citation in the source text; inferred because this is the only printing of this spell in our data.

name: Sunmace
description: A mace forged of pure sunlight springs into being and, at the caster's direction, attacks a designated foe at range every round, dealing 1d8 points of fire damage on a hit (plus 1 per three caster levels, to a maximum of +5 at 15th) and dazzling the target for a round. Against undead the mace instead deals 2d6 fire damage and forces a Will save or blinds the target for a round; undead especially vulnerable to sunlight, such as specters, vampires, and wraiths, take a -2 penalty on that save. It threatens a critical on a natural 20 and deals double damage on a successful critical hit, just like a real mace. It attacks starting the round it's cast and every round after on the caster's turn, using the caster's base attack bonus (which can grant it multiple attacks per round at higher levels) plus their Wisdom modifier; because it strikes as a spell rather than a weapon, it bypasses damage reduction, though it never grants or benefits from flanking, and none of the caster's feats or combat options affect it. If a targeted creature has spell resistance, the mace makes a caster level check against it on its first strike only — if that check fails, the whole spell is dispelled outright, but if it succeeds the mace works normally against that creature for the rest of the duration. The mace itself can't be harmed by physical attacks (its touch AC is 12), though dispel magic, disintegrate, a sphere of annihilation, or a rod of cancellation can affect it, and a deeper darkness spell cast on it instantly dispels it and does nothing else. Each round the caster can use a move action to redirect the mace to a new target — doing so costs it that round's extra attacks, limiting it to a single strike — or leave it attacking whatever it struck the round before; if it ever loses its target, leaves the caster's sight, or goes undirected, it returns to hover near the caster instead.

name: Venomous Volley
description: A cone of venomous spectral fangs bursts from the caster's fingertips, biting everything caught inside for 1d6 points of damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d6); a Reflex save halves this. Anyone struck also suffers a lingering -4 penalty on Fortitude saves against poison for one minute per caster level — an effect that has no saving throw of its own, though spell resistance can still block it. Focus a living snake.

name: Camel's Tenacity
article: Spellcraft – Spell Strips of the Black Pyramid
description: Grants its targets, up to one creature per level, the endurance of a desert beast of burden, letting them go entirely without food or water for as long as the spell lasts (1 day per 3 caster levels). It has no effect against magical dehydration of the kind detailed in Sandstorm, only against ordinary hunger and thirst. Material component a fistful of camel hair.

name: Crushing Coils

targetAreaEffect.value: One snake teleported to constrict target

description: Teleports the caster's serpent focus into any space within medium range, sending it straight at the nearest opponent. Landing in an occupied space lets the snake immediately attempt a grapple that doesn't provoke an attack of opportunity; on a success it establishes a hold and constricts at once, and while the spell lasts it fights with a bonus to its grapple checks and constriction damage equal to half the caster's level, plus DR 10/magic (though it gains no bonus to its attack roll or bite damage). If the initial grapple fails, the snake instead settles into an adjacent empty square and keeps attacking on the caster's turn each round, trying again to establish its improved grapple. As a move action the caster can recall the snake to their side at full speed, then teleport it against a new target as a standard action later in the same spell. Once the spell's duration (1 round/level) runs out, the snake can no longer be teleported and loses its bonuses to grapple checks, constriction damage, and damage reduction. Focus a constrictor snake no more than one size larger than the caster.

name: Detect Defiler
description: Lets the caster sense the presence of defilers, spellcasters who scar the land to fuel their magic, within a cone-shaped emanation out to 60 feet, with the detail revealed increasing the longer the caster concentrates. On the first round it reveals only whether any creature with a defiler score or defiler points is present. On the second round it reveals how many defilers are present and the strength of the most potent aura among them, rated by defiler score: having only defiler points but no score reads as a faint aura, a score of 1-10 as moderate, 11-30 as strong, and 31 or higher as overwhelming. On the third round it pinpoints the power and exact location of every aura present, or just its direction if it's out of line of sight. The caster can redirect their attention to a new area each round. If the single strongest aura present is overwhelming and its source has HD or level at least twice the caster's own, the caster is stunned for a round and the spell ends immediately. The spell can penetrate most barriers, but 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks it entirely — metal barriers and lead sheeting are both rare on Athas, so this limitation matters less there than it might elsewhere.
note: Built entirely around Dark Sun's defiler-score subsystem, which this Greyhawk campaign doesn't use. Mechanically nonfunctional without a DM ruling on whether/how 'defiler score' applies here — flagging for the DM rather than guessing at a houserule.

name: Dust Storm
article: Spellcraft – Spell Strips of the Black Pyramid

targetAreaEffect.value: Sand storm cylinder, 60 ft. across and 30 ft. high

description: Conjures a howling cylinder of wind and sand, 60 feet across and 30 feet high, that obscures vision and injures anyone caught inside. All sight, including darkvision, is blocked beyond five feet: creatures within that inner five feet have concealment (20% miss chance), while anything farther away has total concealment (50% miss chance, with no way to use sight to locate a target at all). Anyone who ends their turn inside the storm takes 1d6 points of slashing damage from the stinging, wind-driven sand.

name: Fang Blade

targetAreaEffect.value: Transforms a snake into a weapon

description: Reshapes the caster's serpent focus into a longsword sized for the caster, its blade glinting with a metallic sheen and its point formed from the snake's own fanged maw; the caster wields it with automatic proficiency as the living steel moves and weaves to aid their grip. On top of normal longsword damage, a hit delivers the source snake's own poison if it's venomous. Only the caster can safely wield the blade — anyone else who tries gets bitten by it instead, at the start of each of their turns, using the original snake's own attack statistics — and it reverts to its living, undamaged form the instant the spell ends. Someone attempting to sunder it treats it as having hardness 8 and the snake's own hit point total at the moment of casting. Focus a live snake no more than one size larger than the caster.

name: Frostbite
description: Inflicts sudden, severe cold damage that mimics prolonged exposure to freezing temperatures: numbness, hypothermia, real frostbite. The target takes 1d6 points of cold damage per two caster levels (maximum 10d6) plus 1d4 points of nonlethal cold damage per two caster levels (maximum 10d4); a successful Fortitude save negates only the nonlethal portion. If the nonlethal damage goes through, the target becomes fatigued.

name: Geyser
description: Blasts a designated target with a jet of pressurized water; a successful ranged touch attack deals 2d6 points of nonlethal damage, plus 1d6 per two caster levels beyond 1st (5d6 at 6th level, 6d6 at 8th, and so on, capping at 8d6 at 12th level and higher). Anyone struck must also save or be knocked prone. It deals no damage at all to objects or to creatures immune to nonlethal damage.

name: Lash of the Kraken
description: Warps one of the caster's limbs into a lashing, barb-covered tentacle straight out of a kraken's arsenal, granting reach and a damage die that scales with the caster's size: 1 point for Fine or Diminutive, 1d3 for Tiny, 1d4 for Small, 1d6 for Medium, 1d8 for Large, 2d6 for Huge, 2d8 for Gargantuan, or 4d6 for Colossal, with reach running from 0 ft. at Fine/Diminutive up through 60 ft. at Colossal. Used as a primary attack it adds the caster's full Strength bonus to damage; used to back up a manufactured weapon as a secondary natural attack it takes the usual -5 penalty instead. A successful tentacle hit lets the caster attempt a grapple without provoking an attack of opportunity, and on a success the tentacle automatically constricts for the same damage again, repeating every round the grapple holds; the grappled foe can escape normally with its own grapple check. A creature that already has a natural tentacle attack can use whichever damage is higher, and gains the ability to grab and constrict with all its tentacle attacks if it couldn't already. The limb reverts to normal when the spell ends (1 minute/level), leaving the caster fatigued for 1d4 minutes afterward.

name: Merrshaulk's Kiss

targetAreaEffect.value: Up to one snake per two levels, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

description: Calls on the serpent god Merrshaulk to bless and enhance up to one living snake per two caster levels, no two of which can be more than 30 feet apart; it affects only true animal-type snakes, never yuan-ti or other snakelike humanoids. Snakes with a poison attack gain a +2 morale bonus to their poison's save DC, snakes with a constrict attack gain a +2 morale bonus on grapple checks, and every affected snake gains a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls, saves, and skill checks. Focus a live snake.

name: Moon's Change
article: Eye of the Night – The Moon and Its Role in D&D
description: Imbues a single touched creature with a rolling tide of enhancement bonuses to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution that builds, peaks, and recedes over the spell's duration (1 round/level). On the first round it grants +2 to all three scores; on the second round, +4; from the third round on it holds at +6 until only two rounds remain, at which point it steps back down to +4, and finally to +2 on the very last round before the spell ends. Material component one drop of blood from a creature with the shapechanger subtype.

name: Moonbridge

targetAreaEffect.value: Bridge, 5 ft. wide and up to 10 ft./level long

description: Solidifies a shaft of moonlight, whether cast naturally by the moon or conjured by a spell like motes of moonlight, into a translucent span the caster and good-aligned creatures can walk across freely. Neutral creatures can also cross, but only while staying in physical contact with the caster — losing that contact drops them — while evil creatures find the bridge as insubstantial as the moonlight it's made of. In open moonlit areas with no distinct shaft of light, the caster can instead conjure a moonbridge from any point within close range. It's always 5 feet wide, at least 20 feet long, and can be extended up to 10 feet per caster level; it can run level or angle up or down along its length by up to a quarter of its total length (rounded down to the nearest 5 feet), as long as the entire span stays bathed in unbroken moonlight. An 11th-level caster, for example, could raise a 110-foot bridge angled as much as 25 feet higher or lower at one end. Material component a vial of pure water bathed in full moonlight for at least six hours.

name: Rain of Terror
description: Calls down a terrifying, unnatural downpour across a 100-foot-radius emanation centered on the caster, its exact form rolled randomly (or chosen outright with a successful DC 20 Concentration check) from a table of eight grotesque possibilities: black, putrid water; ash; steaming blood; toads; dead bats; snakes; spiders; or, on the eighth result, a reroll for a combination of two of the other results (ignoring any further 8s). Everyone but the caster within the area takes a penalty on Will saves against fear effects equal to -1 per four caster levels (maximum -5), while the caster gains a +10 bonus to Intimidate checks for as long as the rain falls. Beyond its terror, the rain behaves exactly like ordinary heavy rain: it halves visibility, imposes a -4 penalty on ranged attacks and on Listen, Spot, and Search checks, automatically douses unprotected flames, and has a 50% chance each round to snuff out protected ones. Any living creatures that fall as part of the rain are genuinely summoned rather than illusory, though the caster has no control over them, they can't actually harm anyone, and only about half of them survive the fall — a rain of toads, for instance, leaves half hopping around and half dead on impact.

name: Rolling Fire

targetAreaEffect.value: Wall of fire, 3 ft. tall and 100 ft. wide

description: Conjures a low, three-foot-tall wall of fire, a hundred feet wide, that scorches anything it touches for 2d6 points of fire damage (Reflex negates), ignites flammable materials on contact, and casts light like a torch. It can be put out in five-foot segments by any means that would douse a normal fire that size. As a move-equivalent action the caster can walk the whole wall up to 30 feet forward or backward along the ground in a straight line — it can climb over barriers shorter than 4 feet but can't cross water or other nonflammable liquid, and it moves as a single unit even if parts of it have already been extinguished. Material component a copper-and-gold comb dusted with ruby powder, worth 1,500 gp as a whole.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor; per the compendium's own rules this spell can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat.

name: Screen of Heat
article: Spellcraft – Spell Strips of the Black Pyramid

targetAreaEffect.value: A screen of heat, up to 10-ft. square/level

description: Conjures an intangible, less-than-an-inch-thick veil of shimmering heat-haze, the kind that warps the horizon on a scorching day, covering up to a 10-foot square per caster level. The caster chooses whether the screen is one-sided or two-sided: a one-sided screen only distorts the view of those looking through it from one direction, leaving the other side unaffected, while a two-sided screen distorts the view from either side equally. Anything viewed through the active face of the screen appears as a wavering, indistinct shape, granting concealment (25% miss chance) to whoever's behind it. A see invisibility spell doesn't cut through the illusion, though true seeing does, and creatures that don't rely on sight to find their targets ignore the screen's effect entirely.

name: Sever Ties of the Moon
description: Loosens a single lycanthrope's bond to the moon, granting it a substantial +10 bonus on all attempts to Control Shape at the cost of fatigue while it holds its hybrid or animal form for the spell's duration (1 minute/level). Returning to humanoid shape clears the fatigue immediately, though it returns the moment the creature shifts back into hybrid or animal form again before the spell ends; it doesn't push an already-fatigued creature into exhaustion.

name: Shooting Star
description: Calls down one or more burning fragments of star from the sky to strike precisely at chosen targets, each dealing 2d6 fire damage with a Reflex save for half. Higher-level casters can call down additional stars, one more for every three caster levels past 3rd, to a maximum of six at 18th, letting several targets be struck in the same casting. The spell fails outright anywhere the sky isn't visible, such as indoors or underground.
note: This entry's printed page (42) has a severely garbled two-column layout around a decorative drop-cap opening that defeated column-order text extraction; the stat block above is confirmed from legible fragments, but one possible secondary mechanical detail (a knockdown effect on a failed save) was too garbled to confirm and was deliberately left out of the description rather than guessed. Material component a chunk of rock and a small glass lens.

name: Snake Shield
description: Grasping the caster's serpent focus, this spell infuses it into a shimmering field of spectral, coiling snakes that spiral tightly around the caster's own body for the duration (1 round/level). Any creature that touches the caster, whether striking with a melee weapon or delivering a touch spell, is bitten by the phantom snakes, which attack using the focus snake's own bite bonus and can bring any of its special attacks (constrict, improved grab, poison) to bear as normal — though a grapple they establish this way can only be held for the one round it's made, not maintained afterward. The snakes can strike a different attacker once per round each, with no cap on how many separate attackers they can retaliate against in a single round. Focus a living snake.

name: Sticks to Snakes
article: Dungeons & Dragons Heroes – Magic, Monsters, and Mayhem
description: Turns a number of dead branches or other slender lengths of wood — arrow shafts, walking sticks, quarterstaffs, and the like — into giant snakes obedient to the caster, up to one stick per four caster levels. The type of snake produced scales with the caster's level: constrictor snakes or large vipers at 8th level or below, huge vipers from 9th–11th, giant constrictor snakes (11 HD) from 12th–15th, giant constrictor snakes (14 HD) from 16th–19th, and gargantuan giant constrictor snakes (20 HD) at 20th or higher. The snakes never attack the caster and can be directed telepathically as a free action to do anything they're physically capable of; left uncontrolled, they simply attack whatever's nearby. Reduced to 0 hit points or less, a snake reverts instantly to its original, undamaged object form.

name: Summon the Pack and Herd

targetAreaEffect.value: Up to 25 creatures per level (see text)

description: A mass-battle escalation of summon nature's ally II: rather than a handful of creatures, it summons twenty-five of a single chosen kind per caster level, restricted to options on the first-level summon list, with no two of the summoned creatures allowed to be more than 100 feet apart. Material component 1,500 gp worth of powdered jet.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor; per the compendium's own rules this spell can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat.

name: Touch of Blibdoolpoolp
article: Spellcraft – Alien Blessings – Spells of Monstrous Deities
description: Reshapes the caster's hand into an oversized, lobster-like claw sacred to the kuo-toa goddess Blibdoolpoolp, granting reach and bludgeoning damage that scales with the caster's size: 1 point for Fine, 1 for Diminutive, 1d3 for Tiny, 1d4 for Small, 1d6 for Medium, 1d8 for Large, 2d6 for Huge, 2d8 for Gargantuan, or 4d6 for Colossal, with reach running from 0 ft. at Fine/Diminutive up to 60 ft. at Colossal. Used alone as a primary attack it adds one and a half times the caster's Strength bonus to damage; used to supplement a manufactured weapon as a secondary attack it takes the usual -5 penalty and adds only half Strength. The claw's grapple bonus scales with size too, from -12 at Fine up to +20 at Colossal, and applies to any disarm, grapple, or trip attempt made with it. A successful claw hit lets the caster attempt a grapple as if one size category larger without provoking an attack of opportunity, and on a success the claw establishes a hold and deals its listed damage again each round the grapple is maintained. A creature that already has its own claw attack can use whichever damage is greater. The caster can't hold objects in the transformed hand or cast spells with somatic components while it's shaped this way, though they still count as armed for the duration (1 minute/level).

name: Desert Burial
article: Spellcraft – Spell Strips of the Black Pyramid
description: A cruel battlefield spell that drags every failed-save creature in a 20-foot-radius spread down into loose ground, burying it up to the neck (or the nearest equivalent for a non-humanoid body) while always leaving it able to breathe. A buried creature is helpless until it beats a Strength or Escape Artist check as a full-round action, with the DC starting at 15 and rising by 1 for every two caster levels the caster possesses; another creature not caught by the spell can aid the escape attempt. While buried, a spellcaster can't cast anything with a somatic or material component unless they already have the material in hand. The spell only affects loose earth such as dirt, mud, or sand — it does nothing to stone, wood, or other solid surfaces — which makes it a favorite opener for creatures wading through shallow water or standing over ground infested with small carnivorous vermin, and a common setup before transmute mud to rock. Material component a paper funnel and a handful of dirt, mud, or sand.

name: Elemental Guardian
article: Ecology – Ecology of the Elemental Weird
description: Conjures a lesser elemental weird to guard a chosen patch of its native element at least 5 feet across. The weird can't move more than 100 feet from that anchor point and can never leave the element it's bound to: a water weird tied to a pond can't leave the pond even within that 100-foot radius, while an air weird can roam freely through open air but still can't fly beyond the same range. It appears in the designated spot and acts immediately, attacking anything but the caster that comes within its reach; if the caster shares a language with it, they can give it more nuanced orders, such as sparing specific individuals or races, or attacking only certain creatures. It obeys those instructions until destroyed or until the spell ends (1 day/level), at which point it departs for its home Elemental Plane. A 15th-level caster can make the binding permanent by following up with permanency at a cost of 3,500 XP, in which case the weird remains until it's destroyed. Material component a bowl or brazier filled with an element matching the weird summoned.

name: Plague Cloud
description: Conjures a sickly gray cloud, heavier than air and thick with disease, across a 100-foot-radius area 20 feet high. At the moment of casting the caster names which disease the cloud carries — blinding sickness, cackle fever, filth fever, mindfire, red ache, the shakes, or slimy doom — and anyone caught inside contracts it immediately on a failed Fortitude save, with no incubation period at all. The cloud drifts with natural or magical wind but has no locomotion of its own, and disperses automatically once the spell's concentration duration ends (up to 1 round/level); anyone already infected stays that way and must recover normally afterward. Material component 3,000 gp worth of crushed amber mixed with dried otyugh blood, sealed inside a small flask.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor; per the compendium's own rules this spell can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat.

name: Spitting Cobra

targetAreaEffect.value: Venom concentrated within the focus snake

description: Distills the venom of the caster's snake focus into a weapon they can spit at range for the duration of the spell (1 minute/level): once per round, as a ranged touch attack out to 120 feet, delivering the focus snake's own poison on a hit exactly as if bitten (with the target allowed the usual Fortitude save, and no extra benefit to the caster from a critical hit). Each attack burns two minutes off the spell's remaining duration, ending the spell early once it would drop to zero or below. The willing source snake loses its own poison bite for as long as the spell lasts. Focus a live, venomous snake no larger than the caster's own size category — a non-poisonous snake causes the spell to simply fail.

name: Dispel War Spell

targetAreaEffect.value: One spellcaster, creature, or object; or a 60-ft.-radius burst

description: Functions exactly as dispel magic, with the addition of a +10 bonus on dispel checks made specifically against spells carrying the war descriptor, and it can be used to counterspell such spells as well. Its full one-minute casting time makes that counterspelling use impractical except against something with an equally slow casting time of at least a minute. Material component sapphires, sunstones, and topazes worth a total of 1,500 gp.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor; per the compendium's own rules this spell can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat.

name: Serpent Storm
description: Fills a 20-foot-radius spread with a storm of deadly snakes that rain down from above and form a dense, writhing carpet across the ground for the duration (1 round/level). Everyone caught inside takes 1d6 points of damage per two caster levels each round from the bites and scratches (Reflex halves), and anyone who takes any of that damage must also succeed at a Fortitude save or be poisoned, taking an initial 1d4 points of Constitution damage with no secondary damage; creatures that avoid all the bite damage avoid the poison too, and anyone who stays in the area keeps rolling fresh poison saves each round. The whole area counts as difficult terrain for as long as the spell lasts. The conjured snakes look exactly like the caster's focus snake but are magical constructs of the spell itself and can't be harmed. Focus one snake no more than one size larger than the caster.

name: Throwing Arm of Iallanis
article: Spellcraft – Alien Blessings – Spells of Monstrous Deities
description: Grants the touched creature the ability to hurl massive stones: a giant rock materializes in one of the target's empty hands the instant the spell is cast (failing outright if it has no free hand), sized and weighted as though thrown by a giant one size category larger than the target. The rock's range increment and damage scale with the target's own size: 120 feet and 2d6 damage at Medium, 140 feet and 2d8 at Large, 160 feet and 3d6 at Huge, 180 feet and 3d8 at Gargantuan, or 200 feet and 4d6 at Colossal. A fresh rock appears in an empty hand at the start of every round the spell lasts (1 round per 5 caster levels), ready to throw the following turn, up to a maximum of four rocks over the spell's duration; the stones are good for nothing but a ranged attack. A target that already has a natural rock-throwing ability gains a flat +4 bonus using these particular stones, stacking with any racial bonus it already has. Small creatures or smaller are beneath the giant deity Iallanis's notice and gain nothing at all from the spell.

name: Revenge of the Land

targetAreaEffect.value: One defiler creature/level, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

description: A druid-only Dark Sun spell channeling the land's own fury against defilers, spellcasters who scar the earth to fuel their magic. Translucent arcs of energy rise from the ground near the caster and connect unerringly to every defiler creature within close range (no two of which can be more than 30 feet apart), dealing 1d8 points of damage per two caster levels each round regardless of whether the target is actually touching the ground. Each affected creature can attempt a Fortitude save every round to negate that round's damage, but must apply its own defiler score as a penalty on the roll. If a target's spell resistance blocks the very first casting, it becomes entirely immune to the spell for the rest of its duration (1 round/level); otherwise it keeps attempting fresh saves each round for as long as it stays within range, with leaving the area or waiting out the duration the only ways to escape the ongoing damage. Creatures with no defiler score at all, including those who have defiler points but no score, are unaffected outright. Material component a live seed, thrown at the caster's feet and ground into the dirt.
note: Like Detect Defiler, this spell is built entirely around Dark Sun's defiler-score subsystem, which this Greyhawk campaign doesn't use. Mechanically nonfunctional without a DM ruling on how (or whether) 'defiler score' maps onto anything in this setting.

name: Curse of Spilt Water
description: On a failed Fortitude save, permanently transforms the target — along with everything it's wearing or carrying — into an equivalent volume of ordinary water, which splashes and spreads across the ground at once, or can be directed by the caster into a suitable container within 5 feet. While transformed the victim has no consciousness and can take no actions whatsoever. Recovering any quantity of the water lets a break enchantment restore the victim to normal, but if the water is allowed to evaporate entirely (a process taking 1 hour for a creature of Fine size, 1 day for Tiny, and 2 additional days for each size category larger than Tiny) or mixes into a larger body of water such as a lake or sea, only a limited wish, miracle, or wish can bring them back. Material component a rag doll soaked in seawater.

name: Lunacy
description: Curses the target with a madness bound to the phases of the moon. From then on, every night of the full moon, the victim rolls d% on a table of compulsions and spends the entire night acting accordingly, regardless of whether the moon is actually visible to them: 01-05 the target simply acts normally; 06-15 (Delusion) it spends the night talking to inanimate objects, refusing to move and finding a new object to address if forced elsewhere, something no ordinary persuasion can stop; 16-25 (Fixation) it moves to a random location in sight and refuses to leave, always trying to return there if dragged away; 26-35 (Flee) it runs at top speed in a random direction for the whole night; 36-50 (Schizophrenia) its alignment flips to its polar opposite for the night (neutral creatures roll randomly for a new one); 51-65 (Catatonia) it collapses and can't be roused by any means; 66-75 (Rage) it methodically smashes every unattended object in sight, spending no more than a minute on any one item before moving to the next; 76-85 (Murderous) it attacks the nearest creature, or goes looking for one if none is present, and nothing short of killing or incapacitating it will stop the violence; 86-95 (Suicidal) it must make an hourly Will save or attempt to kill itself by the fastest means available, taking no other action that turn — an armed target lands an automatic critical hit on itself as a full-round action, while an unarmed one seeks out attacks of opportunity, cliffs, fire, or similar hazards; and 96-100 (Blackout) the DM simply takes control of the character for the rest of the night. At the moment of casting, the caster must name a specific task that alone can end the curse (short of break enchantment, miracle, or wish) — it can't require the victim's own suicide, though it may be dangerous — and the victim always knows exactly what that task is. Material component three drops of blood from a natural lycanthrope.

name: Mire

targetAreaEffect.value: Surface rock in a 60-ft.-radius spread, 10 ft. high

duration: Permanent (see transmute rock to mud in the Player's Handbook)
savingThrow: See transmute rock to mud in the Player's Handbook
description: A battlefield-scale transmute rock to mud, functioning identically to that spell in every respect except its much larger area: a 60-foot-radius spread of surface rock, 10 feet high, rather than a single squad's worth of ground. Material component brown, gray, and black gems worth 7,000 gp total, all of which must be dissolved in acid.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor; per the compendium's own rules this spell can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat.

name: Small Stronghold
description: Conjures a small fortified keep out of solid, magically formed rock — identical to the 'Cheap Keep' described in the Stronghold Builder's Guidebook — whose walls can never be placed so that any solid part of them occupies a creature's space; the structure can enclose creatures within its open interior spaces without harming or trapping them, letting a squadron of soldiers find themselves suddenly walled into a defensible position as the keep rises around them. When the spell ends (1 hour/level) the whole keep collapses to dust, and a dispel magic cast against it only tears down the portion actually caught in that spell's own 30-foot-radius burst rather than the entire structure. Material component 10,000 gp worth of crushed agate, sapphire, and topaz mixed with clay into a model of the keep.
note: Carries the [War] descriptor; per the compendium's own rules this spell can't be acquired or cast without the War Magic Study feat.

name: Submersion Treatment
description: Engulfs the target in a churning column of freezing, swirling water that paralyzes it in the water's grip and deals 1d6 points of cold damage every round it remains inside, though the surrounding liquid also grants a +6 bonus to AC. If the trapped creature is alive and can't breathe water, it can hold its breath for 2 rounds per point of Constitution, after which it must succeed at a Constitution check each round (DC rising by 1 for every previous success) to keep holding its breath; failing that check, or choosing to breathe, drops it unconscious at 0 hit points, then to -1 and dying the following round, and finally drowned on the third. An ally standing outside the column can attempt to end the spell early with a full-round action: a Strength check against a DC equal to the spell's own save DC pulls the trapped creature free. Material component a drop of water and a drop of blood.

name: Dire Reincarnation
description: Functions exactly like reincarnate, except that the returning soul always arrives in the body of a dire animal, determined by rolling d% on the spell's own table: 01-13 dire rat, 14-26 dire weasel, 27-39 dire badger, 40-50 dire bat, 51-59 dire ape, 60-68 dire wolverine, 69-77 dire wolf, 78-84 dire boar, 85-90 dire lion, 91-96 dire bear, and 97-100 dire tiger. Unlike ordinary reincarnate, the deceased's entire body doesn't need to be present — a portion is enough — and the subject can have been dead for far longer, up to a month per caster level rather than a matter of days. As with the standard spell, the reincarnated creature keeps all the movement modes, natural armor, natural attacks, and extraordinary abilities that come with its new dire form. Only a wish or miracle can restore the original body afterward, and even then the reincarnated creature can resist that restoration if it chooses (Will negates). Material component rare oils and unguents worth at least 5,000 gp, spread over the remains.
note: This is this compendium's only Dragon/Dungeon-sourced 8th-level druid spell and the only one of the 44 credited to Dungeon Magazine rather than Dragon Magazine — specifically a web enhancement tied to a Dungeon #100 adventure, not the magazine's print pages.
